locations.note: Colonial Boston, where Connor is drawn into the run-up to the American Revolution.
British-held 18th-century New York, a major battleground in Connor's fight against the Templars.
The Frontier is a major explorable region between the colonial cities.
Naval missions take Connor through the Caribbean.
Connor rides with the militia at Lexington in April 1775.
The fight continues at Concord and the North Bridge.
Connor comes to Philadelphia for the Continental Congress and Washington's appointment as commander.
Connor stands in the crowd beneath the Old State House when the Boston Massacre erupts in March 1770.
The Tea Party: Connor helps the Sons of Liberty dump the tea from Griffin's Wharf in December 1773.
Connor rides with Paul Revere on the night of the lanterns, from the North End out to Lexington.
The Battle of Bunker Hill: Connor crosses the battlefield under fire to assassinate John Pitcairn.
Faneuil Hall and its market, where Connor meets Samuel Adams and the Sons of Liberty.
The Pennsylvania State House, where Connor watches the Continental Congress name Washington commander-in-chief.
Concord Fight: Connor directs the militia's volleys at the North Bridge.
Charles Lee takes refuge in Fort George after Monmouth; Connor infiltrates it and is forced to kill his father, Haytham.
Connor finds Washington's army starving in the winter camp at Valley Forge and learns Lee's part in the Templar plan.
The Battle of Monmouth, June 1778: Connor holds the line as Lee's retreat nearly loses the day for Washington.

routes.name: Connor's war
routes.note: Connor's war runs from the Frontier through Boston, Lexington and Concord, Bunker Hill, New York, Philadelphia, Valley Forge and Monmouth to the final chase at Fort George.
